references.text: Moses gives the same exhortation not to fear the enemy in war, because the Lord is with his people
The Lord tells Joshua not to fear before the battle at Ai, the same encouragement as here
The Lord gives Joshua the same exhortation not to fear before the battle against the five Amorite kings
The command to lame horses is mentioned in connection with the law of kingship in the Mosaic Law
David lamed the horses after victory over Hadadezer, in obedience to this principle
The psalmist contrasts trust in chariots and horses with trust in the name of the Lord
Isaiah warns against trusting in Egyptian horses and chariots instead of the Lord
Moses tells the people not to fear, for the Lord will fight for them against the Egyptians
